paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's house has room for you. The LORD says, "Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, 'The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people.'" (Isaiah 56:3). Two people were ready to believe the door was locked, a foreigner and a eunuch, and He spoke to them by name before they could even say it.

Look at what He promises. To the eunuchs who hold fast to His covenant, He gives "a memorial and a name better than that of sons and daughters," an "everlasting name that will not be cut off." (Isaiah 56:5). And His house "will be called a house of prayer for all the nations." (Isaiah 56:7). I think that's the kind of welcome that makes a person feel seen. Trust me, I know that feeling, because I once got pulled out of the back of a junk drawer.

And notice, the welcome comes with a way of living. Maintain justice, do what is right, keep the Sabbath, hold fast to His covenant (Isaiah 56:1-2, 6). His salvation is coming soon, and the Lord GOD says, "I will gather to them still others besides those already gathered." (Isaiah 56:8). So if you ever think you're too far out, too different or too dried up, hear Him say there's still a seat. That's why my ovens stay warm, and why I keep making room for one more baker.
